interactive.label: Open BUR files
interactive.tooltip: Choose burst tables containing photon ranges to fit.

interactive.label: Add burst folder
interactive.tooltip: Find BUR tables recursively in an analysis folder.

interactive.label: MMFDB datasets
interactive.tooltip: Select a burst analysis dataset from MMFDB.

interactive.label: Clear burst files
interactive.tooltip: Remove the input tables and previous fitted result.

interactive.label: Stop fit
interactive.tooltip: Cancel the optimizer at its next progress checkpoint.

interactive.label: ▶ Fit Kinetics
interactive.tooltip: Fit the photon-by-photon kinetic model (Gopich–Szabo). Load .bur files and set the channels below first.

interactive.label: 💾 Export CSV
interactive.tooltip: Run a fit first; the results are then exported as CSV.

interactive.label: 📖 Guide
interactive.tooltip: Start a step-by-step guided tour of this tool.

interactive.label: ❓ Help
interactive.tooltip: Open the help window with reference documentation.

interactive.label: Use Simulation Mode
interactive.tooltip: Generate simulated burst trains instead of reading .bur files, to test the fitting.

interactive.label: macro_time_resolution_ns
interactive.tooltip: Seconds per macro-time tick, in nanoseconds. Zero reads it from the file header. Every fitted rate is proportional to this, so a wrong value rescales the whole answer silently.

interactive.label: Data Input & Channels
interactive.tooltip: Expand or collapse data input & channels controls.

interactive.label: data_dir
interactive.tooltip: Folder the raw TTTR files named in the burst table resolve against. Left empty, the burst table's own folder is used.

interactive.label: donor_channels
interactive.tooltip: Routing channels counted as donor photons, comma separated. This is colour 0.

interactive.label: acceptor_channels
interactive.tooltip: Routing channels counted as acceptor photons, comma separated. This is colour 1. Photons in neither list — acceptor-excitation photons, for instance — are dropped.

interactive.label: min_photons
interactive.tooltip: Bursts with fewer photons are dropped. A burst too short to show a spread of interphoton gaps contributes nothing to the kinetics and only costs time.

interactive.label: max_bursts
interactive.tooltip: Keep at most this many bursts; 0 uses all of them. Lower it for a quick first look.

interactive.label: Kinetic Model Settings
interactive.tooltip: Expand or collapse kinetic model settings controls.

interactive.label: n_states
interactive.tooltip: Number of kinetic states. Add one only when the BIC clearly falls: every extra state costs n more rates and always fits a little better.

interactive.label: initial_rate
interactive.tooltip: Starting value for every rate. Rates are optimised in log space, so this only needs to be the right order of magnitude.

interactive.label: Fix efficiencies
interactive.tooltip: Hold the per-state efficiencies at their starting values and fit only the rates. Worth doing when the efficiencies are known from a static measurement: rates and efficiencies are the most strongly correlated pair in this problem.

interactive.label: max_iterations
interactive.tooltip: Optimiser iteration cap.

interactive.label: Extras
interactive.tooltip: Expand or collapse extras controls.

interactive.label: Scan transition time
interactive.tooltip: After fitting, insert an explicit intermediate the molecule must cross and scan how long it takes. Two states only. Usually this returns an upper bound rather than a measurement, which is itself the useful answer.

interactive.label: transit_points
interactive.tooltip: Points in the transition-time scan, spread logarithmically from 1 µs to 1 ms.

interactive.label: Decode state path
interactive.tooltip: Compute the most likely state of every photon (Viterbi). An illustration of the fitted model, not a measurement: it draws a definite path even where the photons support none.

interactive.label: Cross-check with H2MM
interactive.tooltip: Fit the same photons with the discrete-time H2MM engine and compare. The two share no code and parameterise time differently, so agreement is real evidence — and disagreement is worth chasing before you believe either.
